2610.13437.title: Local Diagnostics of Learned Event Representations for Anomaly Detection at the HL-LHC
2610.13437.paper_summary: Anomaly detection, the identification of collision events that deviate from Standard Model expectations, is one of the most promising model-agnostic strategies for new-physics searches at the Large Hadron Collider. Searching for rare events in learned low-dimensional representations removes the need to commit to hand-crafted observables a priori, but sacrifices the immediate physical interpretation those observables provide. For anomaly detection to enter a discovery pipeline, flagged events must therefore be diagnosed locally, both to distinguish potential new physics from mismodeling or detector effects and to identify observables for targeted follow-up searches. We evaluate supervised and self-supervised neural embedding strategies on COLLIDE-2V, a 750-million-event dataset simulated under realistic High-Luminosity LHC conditions, using the reconstruction error of an autoencoder trained in the learned latent space as the anomaly score. Across the configurations and benchmark signals considered, supervised objectives, which exploit simulation process labels during training, generally outperform their self-supervised counterparts and, in their best configurations, improve on an autoencoder trained directly on kinematic features, raising the signal efficiency at 10% background acceptance on all held-out processes. We further introduce a local diagnostic pipeline that fits a Gaussian Mixture Model to the SM latent space, profiles each component through high-level observables without process labels, localizes the flagged events, and ranks observables by their local discriminating power. The ranking recovers the defining kinematics of the held-out processes, while correlating the anomaly score with the same observables quantifies how closely the score tracks them, revealing cases where the most discriminating observable is not the one the score follows most closely.
2610.13437.paper_summary_zh: 異常檢測，即識別偏離標準模型預期的碰撞事件，是大型強子對撞機中尋找新物理的最有前景的無模型策略之一。在學習的低維表示中尋找稀有事件消除了事先需要承諾手工製作的可觀測量的必要性，但犧牲了這些可觀測量所提供的立即物理解釋。因此，為了使異常檢測進入發現流程，標記的事件必須在本地進行診斷，以區分潛在的新物理與模型不匹配或探測器效應，並識別可針對後續搜索的可觀測量。我們在COLLIDE-2V上評估了監督式和自監督式神經嵌入策略，該數據集是基於現實的高亮度LHC條件模擬的7.5億事件，使用在學習的潛在空間中訓練的自編碼器的重建誤差作為異常分數。在考慮的配置和基準信號中，監督式目標通常在性能上超過其自監督式對應物，並且在最佳配置下，改善了直接在運動學特徵上訓練的自編碼器，提高了在所有保留過程中以10%的背景接受度的信號效率。我們進一步引入了一個本地診斷流程，該流程將高斯混合模型擬合到SM潛在空間，通過高級可觀測量對每個組件進行分析，而不需要過程標籤，定位標記的事件，並根據其本地區分能力對可觀測量進行排名。該排名恢復了保留過程的定義運動學，同時將異常分數與相同的可觀測量相關聯，量化了分數與它們的跟蹤程度，揭示了最具區分性的可觀測量並不是分數最密切跟隨的那一個情況。
